intended_object: A specific isomorphism (`Fragment.Equiv`) showing that gluing the boundary pairs {i,j} and {k,l} of a fragment gives the same result in either order, up to relabelling. It covers one case of a case analysis ("configuration (2), variant {il}", where one cross-edge joins i and l). This is read off the docstring and the module GlueComm.
explanation:
This is not a mathematical notion that someone would define. It is a proof step that happens to be written as data. It packages the identity flag map, the identity vertex map and a compatibility proof (a five-way case analysis on the partner of a flag) into a `Fragment.Equiv`. The result is that, in this one case, the two orders of gluing an open pair agree.

Its role is a lemma, "the two glues commute in configuration (2, il)". It is stated as a `def` only because `Equiv` is data. The many hypotheses (pairwise distinct labels, openness conditions, the cross-edge condition `hcross`, `hfar_jk`) are exactly the side conditions of this sub-case. They are not part of the definition of any standard object.

So there is no textbook object to compare it against. Its correctness is guaranteed by the type, since the code compiles. Mathlib has no counterpart.
